long_biography.plain_text:
Henk W. Koster became the assignee of a medical-technology patent designed to improve the delivery of therapeutic gases through ventilators. Its system coordinated gas-administration modules with a patient's breathing cycle, using parallel valves and monitoring components to control nitric oxide and other gases precisely. The invention was credited to Dutch engineers Gerard Lugtigheid and Albert Grootendorst, separating Koster's ownership of the patent from their technical authorship.

The patent family reached both European and United States grants around the turn of the century. Its design addressed neonatal and adult applications, tracheal gas insufflation and the measurement of oxygen, nitric oxide and nitrogen dioxide. Koster's role was that of the rights holder, making medical-device intellectual property a documented strand of his business activity.
